real_host_failure_evidence.first_deterministic_blocker: wolfSSL DTLS 1.3 handshake does not complete after the FakeTCP association is established and the Linux DTLS worker is spawned.
real_host_failure_evidence.important_negative_evidence: The old Windows process-order race is removed: DTLS now starts only after FakeTCP READY. No route-apply/connect_pass occurs on this failure, so LINK/TUN/DNS are downstream and not the current blocker.

source_findings.faketcp_client_handshake: Client sends an empty final ACK, initializes sender at ISN+1, then prints READY and starts raw/UDP/retransmit loops. Under the readiness gate, DTLS ClientHello is therefore a normal post-handshake FakeTCP data segment, not final-ACK payload.
source_findings.faketcp_server_mux: After accepting the final ACK, mux starts the per-session DTLS worker and then processes the same segment through HandleSegment. Normal subsequent payload is delivered through sess.relay to the worker socket; server responses are read from sess.relay and enqueued onto FakeTCP raw return traffic.
source_findings.dtls_server: Linux shim prints BOUND before its initial MSG_PEEK, then sets peer, sends an HRR cookie and enters wolfSSL_accept. Existing BOUND alone cannot distinguish blocked MSG_PEEK from a later wolfSSL_accept stall.
source_findings.wolfssl_windows_fd: Pinned wolfSSL 5.9.2 exposes wolfSSL_set_fd(WOLFSSL*, int) and its MSVC SOCKET_T is unsigned int, so WBD's current int cast is consistent with the pinned library API and is not presently treated as the first root cause.
